test_title: PYST 25: SSC MTS 2023 - English (Held On: 14 Sept, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate response in the given situation of the eve of a battle to fill in the blank.

The commander: “Honourable Emperor, all the troops have lined up for the battle and are awaiting your orders.” Emperor Chandragupta Maurya: “_______________.”

options.text: You should learn how to talk to an emperor.
We are ready for the pilgrimage.

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. We will march at dawn. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The word **"march"** means to walk in a military manner with a regular measured tread. (मार्च करना) • **Example: **The soldiers were ordered to march to the battlefield at dawn. • **"dawn" **refers to the first appearance of light in the sky before sunrise; the beginning of a phenomenon or period of time. (भोर) • **Example: **They decided to start their journey at dawn to avoid the heat of the day. • Hence, the phrase **"We will march at dawn" **means the troops will begin their movement or attack at the break of day. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. We will march at dawn. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 2: You should learn how to talk to an emperor.** (तुम्हें यह सीखना चाहिए कि सम्राट से कैसे बात की जाती है) • **Example:** The advisor reprimanded the soldier, saying, "You should learn how to talk to an emperor." • **Option 3: We will be playing cards.** (हम ताश खेल रहे होंगे) • **Example: **Despite the looming battle, the soldiers joked, "We will be playing cards." • **Option 4: We are ready for the pilgrimage.** (हम तीर्थयात्रा के लिए तैयार हैं) • **Example:** The group announced, "We are ready for the pilgrimage," as they prepared to leave. 44:Tbd4, The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Very rarely.
